items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: I used to shine shoes there because the people wanted the Charleston King to shine their shoes.

ctx.x: Was the record store of the Ashford, was that in the black neighborhood?

Yeah, it was on the Central Track. And it was...actually, I don't think he could make it just selling records, do you understand? So he had a shoeshine parlor-- sold shoelaces and things. And he had about seven guys that shined shoes. And I used to shine shoes there because the people wanted the Charleston King to shine their shoes. So you see, all through life I've always tried to figure how to stay one step ahead of the sheriff. (Laughter)

Well those kinds of record stores were still around down South when I was in the army. I was stationed in Georgia--Columbus, Georgia they had those kinds of stores, too. In the front there was a shoeshine parlor and then they'd sell some hushpuppies and...
